consensus.executive_summary: Across the 8 analyzed radiology papers, strong empirical consensus exists that deep learning models achieve high diagnostic discrimination (>88%) under curated or domain-adapted settings. However, a major empirical contradiction divides clean lab studies (Smith 2024: 94.2%) from clinical field deployments (Adewale 2024: 68.4%), where uncalibrated scanner artifacts cause severe diagnostic degradation. Multi-center ensembling and radiologist-in-the-loop workflows consistently outperform autonomous triage.
agreed_findings: Modern neural architectures maintain diagnostic accuracy (>88%) when domain adaptation is applied (Chen 2024, Kowalski 2025).
Pretrained self-supervised adult representations transfer effectively to pediatric radiography with minimal fine-tuning (Dubois 2025).

top_contradictions.headline: Clinical readiness dispute: Smith (2024) reports 94.2% accuracy in clean archives, while Adewale (2024) finds performance drops to 68.4% on field hospital scans.
Human clinician equivalence controversy: Lab benchmark superiority does not hold on noisy field inputs.

recommended_next_steps: Standardize motion-artifact augmentation benchmarks across prospective radiography trials.
Incorporate physical edge hardware thermal constraints into portable triage models.
Mandate radiologist-in-the-loop confidence calibration before autonomous deployment.
